adjudicationCeiling.obligation: #580 body + the 2026-08-13 owner ruling on #580: replace the extrapolated ~1,077-item single-transaction adjudication ceiling with an actual reading from the exec-ledger machinery. #596 recorded the extrapolation; #601 recorded a second, unreconciled ~1,074 for its sibling family and excluded the ceiling from its own scope.
adjudicationCeiling.method: The ceiling is the largest item cardinality N whose NET memory reading — the whole-test row minus its fixture-only control, which is how both cost ledgers already price this walk — is at or below the §3.3 basis. Readings are taken through `onchain/aiken/scripts/run-focused-check.mjs` (the same instrument the ledgers use, which refuses a report assembled from a different module or containing a failure) with the pinned fork. The crossing was located by bisection on the net memory axis over [1,000, 1,100] in a scratch copy of `onchain/aiken`, then the boundary pair was landed as permanent selectors in the measured modules and re-read in place with the ledgers' own control shape.
adjudicationCeiling.notLedgerRows: The four selectors per family are deliberately NOT ledger rows. A within-basis ledger records only rows whose RAW reading fits the basis (`exec-ledger-within-basis-v1.mjs`), and a whole-test reading at these cardinalities is the rule's share plus a fixture that costs about as much again — ~24.2M and ~24.1M memory. What the ledgers publish is the net, which is arithmetic over rows rather than a number the gate checks; these selectors put the crossing on the same footing and additionally pin the SHAPE the reading was taken at, so a change that moves the shape goes red before a published ceiling drifts under an unchanged sentence.

committedFieldShape.shape: §5.1 envelope over N empty items, grammatical, committed at slot 0 where §7.4's `header_len + 40·N` convicts as `wrong_stride`

adjudicationCeiling.reconciliation: The two extrapolations are now two readings, and they genuinely differ: 1,077 for §12.7 against 1,075 for §12.8. The two-item gap is §12.8's higher intercept — the §7.4 stride arithmetic it asks after the same walk. §12.7's fit named the right integer; §12.8's was one item low.
adjudicationCeiling.residualStillExtrapolated: The 29.9x over-basis figure for the worst admissible shape (32,764 / 32,765 minimum-width items at §5.4's byte bound) remains an extrapolation, now taken over the measured boundary pair rather than the 250/500 pair: ~394,200,000 mem for both families (§12.7 and §12.8), the measured marginal being 12,024 mem/item in each; only the fitted slopes separate them. What #580 replaced with a measurement is the ceiling the figure extrapolates past, not the 32,764-item shape itself. The repair on record is §10's resumable walk applied to the verdict.

sixtyFourByteOverhang.obligation: #579 owner ruling 2026-08-14 item 4 — the 64-byte overhang (publication cap 14,396 > tier-1 admissible 14,332) ASSERTED as a #580-inherited gate, 'fails if closed silently'. Asserted at demo/midgard-validation/tests/complete-item-carriage-tiers-emulator-v1.test.ts.
sixtyFourByteOverhang.disposition: REAL, CORRECT, AND NOT A CAPABILITY GAP — the gate stays, unchanged, as an anti-conflation assertion.
reasoning: The two constants answer different questions: 14,396 is the largest complete item ONE PUBLICATION TRANSACTION carries as an inline datum; 14,336 is the largest field preimage a STEP REDEEMER carries. Neither is a bound on the other.

§8.4's ladder is a partition, so nothing in the band is stranded. An item in (14,332, 14,396] has a field preimage in (14,336, 14,400], which selects tier 2 `RawUtxo` — measured green at exactly 14,396 by `carries one complete item at the applied publication maximum through the tier-2 door`, which drives the full authenticate/source/observe/proof journey with every stage inside `maxTxSize`.
The overhang is therefore the tier-1/tier-2 split point sitting 64 bytes below the tier-2/tier-3 split point. That is the ladder working, not a hole in it.

Keeping the assertion is still right, and its value is as an anti-conflation guard: equating the two constants would widen tier-1 acceptance onto a basis the deployed step route does not match — the same soundness-regression shape commit 92426384 refused when it declined to move `maxReliableDirectCompleteItemBytes` from 8,273 to 13,282.
sixtyFourByteOverhang.policyCapChange: NOT required and NOT taken. Per this ticket's brief a policy-cap change is parameter churn to be escalated rather than retargeted; no escalation is raised because no change is needed. Retargeting the tier-1 ceiling upward to close the overhang would be the widening 92426384 refused.
sixtyFourByteOverhang.residual: The 64-byte band is measured only at its upper endpoint (14,396, tier 2) and its lower one (14,332, tier 1). No row drives an item strictly inside the band. That is a coverage observation, not a gap in capability, and it is recorded rather than closed here.
